title: QAdapt: Noise-Adaptive Neural Pre-Decoding for Surface-Code Quantum Error Correction
abstract: arXiv:2607.28422v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Fault-tolerant quantum computing relies on quantum error correction to protect logical information, requiring classical decoders that keep pace with syndrome generation. Heterogeneous, changing hardware noise and the distribution shift from simulation to experiment challenge the accuracy and robustness of fixed neural decoders. We present QAdapt, a noise-adaptive neural pre-decoding framework for surface-code quantum error correction. QAdapt learns local spatiotemporal correlations, continually adapts across noise environments, and passes the residual syndrome to a conventional global decoder. Online elastic weight consolidation limits forgetting as training moves between measurement, idle, CNOT, and Pauli-bias noise regimes. At distance nine, the HTNet pre-decoder reduces equivalent per-round logical error by 15.64% relative to Ising-Fast, with 28.75% fewer parameters and 9.07% less matching-backend time. tldr: QAdapt提出了一种噪声自适应神经预解码框架，通过学习局部时空相关性并结合在线弹性权重巩固，在多种噪声机制间持续适应，显著降低了表面码量子纠错的逻辑错误率并提升了解码效率。
en_tdlr: QAdapt presents a noise-adaptive neural pre-decoding framework for surface-code quantum error correction that continuously adapts to changing noise regimes via online elastic weight consolidation, reducing logical error rates and decoding time.
